summary: OpenAI cut API prices for GPT-5.6 Luna (80%) and Terra (20%), introduced a paid Fast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol replacing Priority Processing, and disclosed serving-side efficiency work (kernel rewrites and token-generation optimizations) behind the price changes.

mechanisms.reason: The document states a concrete technique and figures for reduced compute per token, not just a price cut.
mechanisms.quote: The kernel work helped reduce the end-to-end cost of serving the model by 20%, while its experiments increased token-generation efficiency by more than 15%.

mechanisms.reason: Lower prices are stated to make high-volume workloads economical at greater scale, implying more tokens served in aggregate.
mechanisms.quote: At the lower-cost end, the new Luna and Terra prices make high-volume work economical at much greater scale.

practices.reason: The kernel and token-generation optimizations are described as internal, lab-run infrastructure work, not a recipe an outside team could apply.
practices.quote: Within a human-led process, Sol autonomously rewrote and optimized production kernels, designed and ran hundreds of experiments to improve token generation, and monitored training, intervening when problems arose.

practices.reason: A named benchmark (Agents' Last Exam) is cited to support a cost-performance claim, but it is the lab's own unreplicated comparison.
practices.quote: On professional work, as measured by Agents’ Last Exam, Luna outperforms Fable 5 at an estimated cost per task nearly 99% lower.

practices.reason: Fast mode replaces Priority Processing in the API with backward-compatible tag handling, a naming/interface change teams should be aware of even though it requires no migration work.
practices.quote: Fast mode is backward compatible: requests tagged priority will automatically use Fast mode.

practices.reason: The document states a stated cost and speed improvement for Luna relative to prior frontier-class models, relevant to teams optimizing cost-sensitive workloads.
practices.quote: Luna delivers performance comparable to models that were frontier-class a year ago at roughly 6 cents on the dollar per task, and at nearly nine times the speed.

notable_reason: An 80% price cut on a widely-deployed model tier, paired with disclosed serving-level efficiency gains (20% cost reduction, 15% token-generation efficiency), is a concrete inference-economics data point worth tracking.
